summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including morbid obesity, chronic lymphedema, recurrent cellulitis, seizure disorder, obstructive sleep apnea, and chronic kidney disease was admitted for worsening bilateral leg swelling, pain, and erythema following a ruptured blister on her right leg. Initial concern for cellulitis was reconsidered after dermatology and infectious disease evaluations found no clear infection; antibiotics were discontinued. The primary issue was determined to be a flare of lymphedema, managed with increased diuresis using bumetanide 4 mg daily and IV furosemide as needed. Her pain, exacerbated by swelling, was managed with continued home opioids and IV morphine during hospitalization, with a plan to resume only oral medications at discharge. She experienced a complex partial seizure during admission, which was managed with ongoing levetiracetam and topiramate. Warfarin was adjusted to 9 mg daily to achieve therapeutic INR. She declined further imaging for edema workup due to claustrophobia. By discharge, her legs had improved significantly, weight decreased, and inflammation markers normalized. She was discharged home with services, on optimized diuretic and anticoagulant regimens, with follow-up plans including a heart failure specialist referral and smoking cessation support.
problems: Localization-related (focal) (partial) symptomatic epilepsy and epileptic syndromes with complex partial seizures, not intractable, without status epilepticus
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease with stage 1 through stage 4 chronic kidney disease, or unspecified chronic kidney disease
Morbid (severe) obesity due to excess calories
Personal history of other venous thrombosis and embolism
Personal history of malignant neoplasm of other female genital organs
